title: Three Turn-Around Stocks I'm Buying Today
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
summary: Joseph Carlson spent $5,000 on three turnaround buys, framing each as a high-quality business priced like a dying one. Netflix: he added $2,000 to an existing $88,000 position (6% of portfolio); the stock trades at $67, down ~50% from $122 highs, at an 18.5x forward PE, with revenue growing 10%+ in every region, 24% organic EPS growth (5.8% reported including the one-time Warner Bros. payout), and $11B trailing free cash flow. He argues the Warner Bros.-Paramount merger's $80-90B debt mountain forces content licensing onto Netflix (Disney already licensing its best content there), and rebuts the engagement/content-quality myths via the Ben Affleck correction of the Matt Damon plot-restatement story. Uber: he bought $2,000 at $69 (down 30% YTD); 17x forward PE, ~5-6% FCF yield; robo-taxi disruption fears are overpriced — Uber does 297M weekly rides versus Waymo's 500k and is growing faster, staying profitable even in San Francisco. S&P Global: he added $1,000 to a $114,000 position (down 24% YTD on Anthropic-plugin 'SaaS apocalypse' fears); ratings and indices are wide-moat, high-margin businesses, and ETF AUM doubling from $3T to ~$6T since 2023 plus a debt-refinancing wall support activity. He passes on Nike (revenue $51B to $45B, declining EPS, fading brand) and stays on the fence on FICO (great fundamentals, but CEO selling and self-inflicted moat damage). Also covered: a Tom Lee bullish market interview and Apple as 'fail of the week' for tightening Mac AI-agent data controls to defend its App Store toll booth against Meta's Muse. Calls: NFLX BUY @ $67 (FLIP from HOLD Oct 2), UBER BUY @ $69 (reiterated), SPGI BUY (adding, reiterated), NKE AVOID (first call), FICO UNCERTAIN.
